title: Pilates Instructor Salary: Hourly Rates, Annual Pay, and Award Guide 2026
description: Discover the pilates instructor salary under the Fitness Industry Award. Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual pay, including casual loading, super, and tax for 2026.
salarySummary: A full-time pilates instructor at Level 3 under the Fitness Industry Award earns $27.97 per hour, or approximately $55,290 per year based on a 38-hour week, plus super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a pilates instructor in Australia?
faqs.a: Under the Fitness Industry Award (MA000094), the minimum hourly rate for a Level 1 adult employee is $25.74 per hour (full-time or part-time). A pilates instructor with higher qualifications may be classified at Level 3 ($27.97) or Level 4 ($30.66). Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, so a Level 1 casual earns $32.18 per hour. These rates apply from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a full-time pilates instructor working 38 hours per week at Level 3 ($27.97), the calculation is: $27.97 × 38 × 52 = $55,289.72 per year. This is gross pay before tax and does not include superannuation, which is paid on top at 12% of ordinary earnings.

faqs.q: Does a casual pilates instructor get paid more?
faqs.a: Yes. Casual employees under the Fitness Industry Award receive a 25% casual loading on the base hourly rate. For example, a Level 1 casual earns $32.18 per hour compared to $25.74 for a permanent employee. The loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave. When calculating annual pay, use the casual rate in the same formula: $32.18 × hours per week × 52 to estimate gross annual income.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Pilates Instructor Salary in Australia

If you are looking for a **pilates instructor salary** guide, the starting point is the award that covers the fitness industry. Most pilates instructors in Australia are covered by the **Fitness Industry Award (MA000094)**, which sets minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes a pay guide for this award, updated after the Annual Wage Review each year. From 1 July 2026, award rates increased by 4.75%, and the National Minimum Wage rose to $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. However, a pilates instructor working in a gym, studio, or fitness centre is almost always covered by the Fitness Industry Award. The award has seven classification levels. A new instructor might start at **Level 1** ($25.74 per hour), while a more experienced or qualified instructor could be at **Level 3** ($27.97) or **Level 4** ($30.66). These rates are for full-time and part-time adult employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of these base rates.

For example, a Level 3 full-time pilates instructor earns $27.97 per hour. The weekly rate for 38 hours is $1,062.90, and the fortnightly pay is $2,125.80. The annual gross salary is approximately $55,290. This is above the National Minimum Wage, which is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week.

### Converting Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

The standard formula to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a full-time week of 38 hours. If you work part-time or casual hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. For a casual pilates instructor at Level 1 ($32.18 per hour) working 20 hours per week, the annual estimate would be $32.18 × 20 × 52 = $33,467.20.

Remember that this formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It is a starting point for budgeting.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees under the award get a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. The loading is already included in the casual rates shown in the pay guide. When you use the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman, you will see separate tables for permanent and casual employees.

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time Level 3 pilates instructor earning $55,290, the super contribution would be $6,634.80 per year. The employer pays this amount to your super fund, not deducted from your pay.

### Tax on a Pilates Instructor Salary

Income tax for the 2026–27 financial year uses the resident tax scale:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,001

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (single reduction thresholds not confirmed for 2026–27). For a $55,000 salary, the tax plus Medicare would be roughly $7,656. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculators to get a more precise estimate.

### Using the Fair Work Commission Data

The Fair Work Commission provides the **Modern Awards Pay Database** with accurate minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates. The Fitness Award pay guide includes all classifications, allowances like first aid ($3.40 per day), leading hand, and vehicle allowance ($1.00 per km). These are not included in the base rate.

For more detailed classification, see the [reference tables](/data) from the Fair Work Commission.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is the average pilates instructor salary?
The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average full-time adult ordinary time earnings at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That includes all industries. A pilates instructor under the award is likely lower than that average. A Level 3 instructor at $27.97 per hour is below the national average.

#### How does casual loading affect annual pay?
When you use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, you can enter the base rate and check the casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. The tool has a checkbox to add 25% on top.

#### What about super and packaging?
Super is paid on top of your gross pay. The employer pays 12% of ordinary earnings. Salary packaging is not included in the annual estimate. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging] for more details.

### Conclusion

A pilates instructor salary depends on classification, hours, and employment type. Use the award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission to ensure you are paid correctly. Use the formula to convert hourly to annual, and remember super and tax to estimate your take-home pay.
